plain:
This task is ROADMAP.jsonl entry `042`. Mark it `in_progress` before doing anything else — Foreman's picking flow deliberately leaves it `planned` until you do:
`echo '{"id":"042","status":"in_progress"}' | node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/roadmap.js update-status`
Then take the commit boundary before touching any file:
`node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/safe-commit.js begin`
Keep its `baseline.head`. A `dirty:true` result means the tree already carries someone else's changes: tell the user in one line, then do the work and make NO commit at all — leave everything in the tree for them. Never stage around it.
When the work concludes, close the entry the same way — the status it actually earned (`done`, `dropped`, `rejected`) and your full findings in `notes`.
Stage the task's own files with the safe-commit primitive — never `git add -A`:
`echo '{"id":"042","expected":["<the files this task owns>"]}' | node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/safe-commit.js finish --baseline <baseline.head> --no-commit`
Then close with `staged:true` (the script folds the staged files into `observed_touches` and stages ROADMAP.jsonl alongside), then commit once with `Foreman: 042` as the final line of the message.
`echo '{"id":"042","status":"<status>","staged":true,"notes":"<findings>"}' | node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/roadmap.js update-status`
Also add `model` and `effort` to that close call — what actually ran this task. Record a Claude model by its family label: `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus` or `fable`. Omit either one you genuinely don't know rather than guessing — an absent field reads as unrecorded, a wrong one silently poisons the corpus.
